parts:
Hello,

 This is my first posting to this group. I apologize if it has been answered earlier.

 I am using MethylKit to analyze RRBS data from zebrafish. I am trying to draw the bar plot using diffMethPerChr and I am finding it hard to exclude some of the data points. Zebrafish genome has lot of contigs and scaffolds (Zv9_scaffold number) that do not have any methylation coverage. I tried to use exclude = ("Zv9_*") but it is not working. I tried to giving exclude =("chr1") and that also doesn't work.

 Any help would be highly appreciated it. In addition, I would like to know if ideoDMC (which is in a blog) will be incorporated into the package.

Here is what I am trying to do.

myDiff=calculateDiffMeth(meth)
myDiff25p=get.methylDiff(myDiff, difference=25,qvalue=0.01)
diffMethPerChr(myDiff, plot=FALSE, qvalue.cutoff=0.01, meth.cutoff=25, exclude=("chr1"))

Here is a syntax that should work for you:

diffMethPerChr(subsethyper,plot=T, exclude = levels(subsethyper$chr)[c(1,26:890)])

I am assuming that you want to exclude every contig that starts with "z" and "Z" and "*" and "chrM". I leave it to you to explore why this works and why your prev command doesn't work!
ᐧ

Regards,
Kalyan

Hi Tuba,

if you used the myDiff25p.hypo object to generate the diffAnn.hypo object, then yes, in theory, they should have the same number of rows. However, only 25634 of your 25707 sites could be assigned to a TSS. A simple reason for not finding a TSS-CpG association could be that there is no annotated gene on the given contig for your genome. 
The direct mapping between the two files is given by the 'target.row' column of tss.assoc.hypo, which contains the original row number of myDiff25p.hypo. Using this column, you should be able to figure out which rows are are missing and which contigs failed. 

I hope this helps. 

Best,
Alex

Hi Tuba, 

Your annotated object "diffAnn.hypo/hyper"  includes a binary membership matrix telling you if a CpG was annotated as promoter, exon or intron. You can access this matrix using the getMembers function and use it to subset your original myDiff.hypo/hyper objects.

Hi Tuba,

if you used the myDiff25p.hypo object to generate the diffAnn.hypo object, then yes, in theory, they should have the same number of rows. However, only 25634 of your 25707 sites could be assigned to a TSS. A simple reason for not finding a TSS-CpG association could be that there is no annotated gene on the given contig for your genome. 
The direct mapping between the two files is given by the 'target.row' column of tss.assoc.hypo, which contains the original row number of myDiff25p.hypo. Using this column, you should be able to figure out which rows are are missing and which contigs failed. 

I hope this helps. 

Best,
Alex

Hi Tuba,

if you used the myDiff25p.hypo object to generate the diffAnn.hypo object, then yes, in theory, they should have the same number of rows. However, only 25634 of your 25707 sites could be assigned to a TSS. A simple reason for not finding a TSS-CpG association could be that there is no annotated gene on the given contig for your genome. 
The direct mapping between the two files is given by the 'target.row' column of tss.assoc.hypo, which contains the original row number of myDiff25p.hypo. Using this column, you should be able to figure out which rows are are missing and which contigs failed. 

I hope this helps.

Alex
